selection: Eight historical disclosures/research sources; seven GitLab-hosted HackerOne report mirrors and one PortSwigger primary research article. Curated examples, not exhaustive coverage or current vulnerability claims.

H1-582349.title: Last pipeline status for MR leaked
H1-582349.author: xanbanx
H1-582349.observation: A merge-request status endpoint exposed pipeline information despite a separate pipeline visibility restriction.

H1-1758126.title: Maintainer can leak webhook secret token by changing the webhook URL
H1-1758126.author: joaxcar
H1-1758126.observation: Changing a webhook destination allowed a maintainer to receive a stored secret that the interface no longer revealed.

H1-427364.title: SSRF in Prometheus integration
H1-427364.author: bull
H1-427364.observation: An initially external integration URL redirected to an internal destination without the destination restriction being reapplied.

H1-470309.title: Bypass MR approval count by exploiting race condition in merge request approval
H1-470309.author: flashdisk
H1-470309.observation: Concurrent approval submissions allowed the same participant's approval to count more than once.

H1-881798.title: Bypass GitLab public and commit email addresses changing validation
H1-881798.author: enumzero
H1-881798.observation: Simultaneously updating email fields let equality with a newly changed address substitute for verified ownership. This does not by itself establish a concurrency bug.

H1-1398305.title: Stored XSS on issue comments and other pages which contain notes
H1-1398305.author: jarij
H1-1398305.observation: Rendering transformations and custom-element handling provided sanitization bypasses in stored note content.

H1-3257843.title: Client Side Path Traversal leads to CSRF token leakage and ATO on self-hosted instances
H1-3257843.author: swiftee
H1-3257843.observation: An unencoded branch identifier altered a frontend request path and chained into a redirect. The report distinguishes a CSP-blocked hosted deployment from affected self-hosted conditions.

PS-CACHE-ENTANGLEMENT.title: Web Cache Entanglement: Novel Pathways to Poisoning
PS-CACHE-ENTANGLEMENT.author: James Kettle
PS-CACHE-ENTANGLEMENT.observation: Bug bounty case studies show how cache-key omissions and differences in request interpretation can hide input effects or reuse changed responses across requests.

checks.title: Authorization on sibling and summary endpoints
checks.applicability: A protected resource has status, preview, export, search, or summary endpoints.
evidence: Resource visibility policy and two controlled roles
Captured main and sibling requests
Policy and response projection code
inspect: Compare permission checks across entry points.
Trace derived fields back to protected objects.
Inspect global policy before concluding a check is missing.
steps: Establish permitted access to a disposable object.
Compare main and sibling views using a denied test principal.
Check restricted fields, including metadata, against the policy.
checks.expected: Every representation respects the underlying resource's visibility policy.
checks.regression: Pair permitted and denied cases across all representations.
checks.caution: A publicly intended summary is not a leak; a shared identifier alone proves nothing.

checks.title: Stored credentials bound to editable destinations
checks.applicability: A webhook or integration combines a hidden credential with an editable URL.
evidence: Secret-access and destination-edit policies
Configuration change and dispatch requests
Credential binding and outbound client code
inspect: Separate permission to use a secret from permission to reveal it.
Check destination changes, redirects, and credential reuse.
Inspect whether changing origin invalidates or reauthorizes the credential.
steps: Configure a dummy secret and controlled receiver.
Using the test editor role, change to a second controlled receiver.
Trigger one test delivery and inspect which credentials arrived.
checks.expected: Destination changes cannot reveal credentials outside their permitted trust boundary.
checks.regression: Test origin changes with dummy credentials and both permitted and restricted editors.
checks.caution: Some editors are intentionally entitled to the secret; establish policy before reporting.

checks.title: Outbound destination checks after redirects
checks.applicability: The server fetches a configurable integration, import, preview, or webhook URL.
evidence: Outbound destination policy
A captured fetch configuration or request
URL validation, redirect handling, and connection code
inspect: Determine which component actually follows redirects.
Check validation at each destination transition.
Inspect address resolution and deployment egress restrictions.
steps: Establish a fetch to a controlled receiver.
In an isolated environment, redirect to a controlled destination forbidden by the test policy.
Correlate receiver logs to determine whether the restricted hop was requested.
checks.expected: Destination restrictions hold across every followed redirect.
checks.regression: Cover accepted initial destinations and denied redirect destinations.
checks.caution: An outbound callback alone proves fetching, not access to protected services.

checks.title: Duplicate approval and one-time action races
checks.applicability: Approvals, redemption, or one-time transitions rely on a count or uniqueness rule.
evidence: The unique-actor or one-use invariant
Baseline operation and resulting state
Transaction, uniqueness, and idempotency implementation
inspect: Locate the check and state update.
Check database enforcement rather than only UI guards.
Inspect worker retries and actor identity binding.
steps: Record the initial state of a disposable object.
In an isolated test, compare sequential repetition with a bounded pair of concurrent requests.
Verify persisted distinct actors and effects after processing completes.
checks.expected: Repeated requests cannot satisfy a distinct-actor or one-use requirement.
checks.regression: Assert the invariant under retries and bounded concurrency.
checks.caution: Two successful responses need not mean two effects; one unsuccessful race attempt is inconclusive.

checks.title: Verified identity versus mutable profile fields
checks.applicability: A profile update changes identity fields used for verification or trust decisions.
evidence: Which identity attributes require verification
Captured profile update and resulting state
Binding, validation order, and verified-identity storage
inspect: Distinguish persisted verification from equality between input fields.
Follow combined updates in their actual order.
Identify downstream features relying on the changed attributes.
steps: Use a test account and an owned but unverified address.
Compare separate and combined updates of related fields.
Verify stored verification state and access to a feature requiring it.
checks.expected: Updating matching fields cannot manufacture verified ownership.
checks.regression: Cover combined changes, unverified addresses, and valid verified transitions.
checks.caution: Unverified display text may be intentional. Do not label a same-request ordering flaw a race without concurrency evidence.

checks.title: Sanitization followed by rendering transformations
checks.applicability: Stored user content passes through Markdown, highlighting, custom elements, or HTML rendering.
evidence: Storage and display requests
Sanitizer, transformation order, and final DOM sink
Browser origin, CSP, sandbox, and viewer context
inspect: Trace transformations after sanitization.
Check escaping for the final attribute or HTML context.
Inspect browser-side processing and actual isolation boundaries.
steps: Save a harmless marker in a controlled test object.
Inspect server output and resulting DOM with a second test viewer.
If appropriate, verify harmless local execution and its origin without reading credentials.
checks.expected: Every transformation preserves the intended non-executable content boundary.
checks.regression: Exercise the complete rendering pipeline and supported browser contexts.
checks.caution: Reflection or HTML insertion is not execution; CSP and sandbox can materially limit impact.

checks.title: Frontend identifiers changing request destinations
checks.applicability: Frontend code inserts a user-controlled name or identifier into an authenticated request URL.
evidence: Frontend URL construction and request headers
Captured browser request and redirect chain
CSP, CORS, and intended destination policy
inspect: Check component encoding before interpolation.
Follow browser normalization and redirect handling.
Determine where credentials or custom tokens can be sent.
steps: Use a disposable named object and harmless path markers.
Observe the browser's actual normalized destination.
With dummy tokens and a controlled receiver, verify any proposed destination/credential chain.
checks.expected: Identifiers remain path data and cannot redirect authenticated operations across trust boundaries.
checks.regression: Cover encoded delimiters, actual browser requests, and deployment restrictions.
checks.caution: Do not transfer the historical account-takeover impact: each redirect, header, browser, and policy dependency needs evidence.

checks.title: Cache keys versus application input interpretation
checks.applicability: A shared cache fronts responses influenced by request inputs or identity.
evidence: A verified isolated cache namespace
Paired requests and cache/origin observations
Cache-key configuration and application input parsing
inspect: Compare inputs affecting content with inputs included in the cache key.
Check normalization at each layer.
Determine whether headers, query, or body are interpreted differently.
steps: Establish isolation; do not assume a random query parameter changes the cache key.
Use a harmless marker and a controlled follow-up request without it.
Correlate repeated responses with cache behavior and origin logs.
checks.expected: Responses are reused only for requests with equivalent security-relevant inputs.
checks.regression: Test differing inputs and principals through the deployed cache configuration.
checks.caution: Reflection, timing, or a HIT header alone is insufficient. Without verified isolation, record a gap and stop the cache test.
